findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed at least two employees use their bare hands to turn off faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed with person-in-charge proper handwashing techniques. See that all employees are educated on correct handwashing procedures. Always use a barrier (paper towel) to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. This prevents recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system were starting to accumulate with grease debris. The PIC mentioned that the facility usually cleans the baffles manually in the triple sink. Discussed cleaning the baffles more frequently to avoid grease accumulation. Also discussed hiring a third party company to service the internal duct work of the hood system. Ensure that hood system is serviced as often as necessary.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a few broken floor tiles throughout the kitchen area. Shown to PIC the specific areas. Either seal broken tiles or repair. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Not all employees working at the time of the inspection had food handler certificates. Discussed with PIC that all employees will need to have at least a food handler certificate if not a certified food protection manager. Ensure that every employee obtains a food handler certificate if handling food or clean dishes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were several different time/temperature control (TCS) foods stored in the standing coolers and the pizza cooler that lacked proper date marking. These TCS foods include sliced deli meats, soft cheeses, tomato sauces, etc. Discussed the need of date marking for TCS foods held in house longer than 24 hours. Ensure that TCS foods that will be cold held longer than 24 hours are date marked with the date that it is opened or prepared. Be sure to discard if not used within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There were stacks of single service items such as portion cups and salad containers that were observed with the food contact surface turned upward on a storage shelf. Discussed with PIC that single service items should be inverted, where the food contact surface is not exposed to contamination. Ensure that single service items are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Floors and walls throughout the facility is in need of deep cleaning. Observed food debris along the back wall behind where pizza dough is prepped and also underneath pieces of equipment and prep tables. Discussed with PIC. When time permits, be sure to pull pieces of equipment from walls to wipe down floors and walls.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a few broken floor tiles throughout the kitchen area. These areas included under the handwashing sink, to the left of the standing coolers, and in open floor areas. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. The only CFPM wasn’t available during the inspection. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation.  

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.
